description: We are Team RimotilyNet, a team of innovators passionate about bridging the digital divide through technology. We are developing a solar-powered, offline-first network that provides rural communities with educational resources, NASA Earth data, and digital services. Our interests include software development, networking, renewable energy, and space technology. We welcome teammates skilled in Next.js, IoT, Raspberry Pi, networking, UI/UX, GIS, and problem-solving to help bring our vision to life.
summary:
RimotilyNet is an innovative, solar-powered, offline-first community connectivity solution designed to bridge the digital divide in underserved rural communities, beginning in Lira, Uganda.

The project combines a locally hosted digital platform, wireless networking, offline educational resources, and NASA Earth observation data to make essential information accessible even where internet connectivity is unreliable or unavailable.

Using Next.js, JavaScript, SQLite, and a Raspberry Pi-based network architecture, we developed a software prototype that brings together educational resources, a community communication platform, and a climate dashboard integrating NASA POWER data on temperature, precipitation, and surface soil wetness.

Our proposed deployment uses solar-powered wireless access points to extend access to schools, health centres, and farming communities. Climate information is synchronized when internet connectivity is available and stored locally for offline access.

RimotilyNet demonstrates how space-based information, affordable computing, renewable energy, and locally accessible digital services can work together to support education, climate awareness, and community resilience.
details:
RimotilyNet: Connecting Communities Beyond the Internet

The Problem

Access to reliable internet remains a major challenge in many rural communities across Uganda. Schools struggle to obtain digital learning materials, farmers have limited access to useful climate information, and community institutions face barriers to sharing knowledge and essential information.

Conventional internet infrastructure can be expensive, unreliable, and difficult to maintain in remote locations. This creates a persistent digital divide between connected urban centres and underserved rural communities.

RimotilyNet addresses this problem by rethinking connectivity: instead of requiring continuous internet access, we designed a system that makes valuable digital resources available locally, even when the internet is disconnected.

Our Solution

RimotilyNet is a proposed solar-powered community network supported by an offline-first digital platform. The system uses a Raspberry Pi as a local server, wireless access points to distribute connectivity, and a web application through which community members access information.

The solution brings together four essential services:

1. Offline Educational Library

RimotilyNet integrates with Kiwix, an offline content platform that can provide educational materials, reference information, and other digital learning resources without requiring an active internet connection.

2. NASA Climate Information Dashboard

Our platform integrates NASA POWER Earth observation data to provide information on temperature, precipitation, and surface soil wetness.

The application is designed to synchronize available NASA data whenever internet connectivity is restored, store the records locally, and make previously downloaded information accessible offline.

For farmers and community institutions, these historical climate observations can support climate awareness, agricultural planning, and informed discussions about environmental conditions. They are not presented as real-time forecasts.

3. Community Communication

RimotilyNet includes a local messaging board where students, teachers, community mentors, and other users can exchange questions and information within the local network.

4. Local Network Administration

The system architecture includes network administration capabilities for monitoring the availability of local digital services and supporting future deployments.

How It Works

The proposed main hub consists of a Raspberry Pi running local server software and hosting the RimotilyNet application.

Community members connect using Wi-Fi-enabled devices and access the platform through a local network address.

The application serves locally available educational resources, cached NASA observations, and community discussions without depending on continuous internet connectivity.

When an internet uplink becomes available, the system can retrieve updated NASA information and store it for future offline access.

For wider community coverage, the proposed deployment uses outdoor wireless access points, with solar power and battery storage supporting operation in areas with unreliable electricity.

Technologies and Tools

  • Next.js, React, TypeScript, and JavaScript for the web application
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive interface design
  • Node.js for server-side operations
  • SQLite for local data storage
  • NASA POWER API for Earth observation data
  • Kiwix for offline educational content
  • Raspberry Pi 4 as the proposed local server
  • Ubiquiti wireless access points for the proposed community network
  • Solar photovoltaic panels and battery storage for the planned power system

Innovation and Creativity

RimotilyNet's innovation lies in combining localized connectivity, offline digital services, renewable energy, and NASA Earth observation information into one community-focused system.

Unlike platforms that become inaccessible when the internet fails, RimotilyNet is designed to preserve access to locally stored content and services.

Its modular approach also allows the network and services to expand as additional hardware, funding, and community partnerships become available.

Development Status

During the project development process, we created a Next.js application starter, a NASA data synchronization module, a local database structure, community messaging functionality, and technical documentation for the proposed Raspberry Pi deployment.

The physical solar-powered wireless network remains a proposed deployment architecture requiring hardware integration, field testing, and validation.

Intended Impact and Scalability

RimotilyNet initially targets underserved communities in Lira, Northern Uganda, with opportunities for expansion into other districts and regions.

The project aims to improve access to educational resources, increase the availability of climate information, facilitate community knowledge-sharing, and reduce dependence on continuous internet connectivity.

Our long-term vision is to develop an affordable, locally maintainable digital infrastructure model that helps rural communities access knowledge and opportunities regardless of their location.
